: JUDGMENT:

Petitioners filed Claim Petition U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act claiming compensation of Rs.35,00,000/- for the death of Sandeep L S, in road traffic accident occurred on 13.04.2023.
2.

The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 13.04.2023 at about 9.45 a.m., Sandeep was proceeding by riding Honda Activa Bike bearing No. KA.11.EK.5856 on Halaguru-Channapattana road, near Naripura village, at that time the driver of the Ashoka Layland Goods Vehicle bearing No.
KA.42.A.9194 came from Halaguru side towards Channapattana at high speed, in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the vehicle in which Sandeep was proceeding and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, Sandeep sustained grievous head injuries.

Immediately, injured was shifted to Halaguru Government Hospital, after first aid he was shifted to Chandramma Dayananda Sagar hospital,
Harohalli and later he took treatment at Victoria hospital as an inpatient.
But in spite of treatment also injured succumbed to the accidental injuries on 14.04.2023.
Thereafter postmortem was conducted in the said hospital, dead body was handed over to the petitioners.
The petitioners have shifted the body to their place and performed funeral and obsequies ceremonies by spending an amount of Rs.1,00,000/-.
Prior to the accident, deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 35 years, doing agricultural work and also electrician work and thereby earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
The deceased has contributed his entire income to the welfare of the family.
Due to death of deceased, petitioners have lost their earning member of the family.

Further, the accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the Ashok Leyland Goods Vehicle bearing Reg.No. KA.42.A.9194 by its driver and in this regard Thayamma vs Ameer Jan.S on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103404878/
2 Halaguru police have registered the case in Cr.No.56/2023 against the driver of the said vehicle for the offence punishable under Sec.279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC.
At the time of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
With these averments they prayed to allow the petition.
3. In response to the notice issued by the Tribunal, both the respondents have appeared before the tribunal through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements.

4. The written statement averments of 1st respondent is as hereunder:
This respondent has denied the cause and manner of accident by contending that the rider of the Bullet Bike came to the extreme right side with heavy speed and dashed against the Ashok Leyland Goods vehicle and caused the accident.
Further it has denied the age, occupation and income of the deceased.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners is excessive and exorbitant.

This respondent has admitted that, the offending Ashok Leyland Goods vehicle bearing No. KA.42.A.9194 is insured with 2nd respondent insurance company and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
With these grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. The written statement averments of 2 nd respondent is as hereunder:
This respondent has contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant and without any basis.
Further it has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of Ashok Leyland Goods vehicle bearing No. KA.42.A.9194 and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.

Further contended that, the accident was caused due to the negligence of the deceased himself who was riding the motor cycle without wearing helmet and without having valid driving license and policy as on the date of accident.

Further it has also contended that the driver of the offending Ashok Leyland Goods vehicle bearing No. KA.42.A.9194 was not having valid driving license as on the date of accident and hence violated the policy conditions.
Further it has denied the age, occupation and income of the deceased.
Further contended that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
With these grounds, the 2nd respondent prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the tribunal has framed the following:
: I S S U E S:
1.

Whether petitioners proves that Sandeep L S was died on 14.04.2023 in the accident occurred on 13.04.2023 at 9.45 a.m. near Nareepura village, on Halaguru - Channapatna road, due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Ashok Layland Lorry bearing No. KA.42.A.9194 as stated in the petition?

Thayamma vs Ameer Jan.S on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103404878/
3
2. Whether the petitioners prove the age and income of the deceased?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation? If so, how much and from whom ?
4. What order or award?
7. In order to prove the case of the petitioners, 2 nd petitioner got examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.17.
P.W.1 was cross-examined from the side of respondent No.2.
Per contra, in spite of sufficient opportunity respondents have not lead any evidence.
8. Heard the arguments from both side.
Perused the records placed before the court.

The findings of this Tribunal on the above referred Issues are as hereunder:-
Issue No.1 :- In the Affirmative Issue No.2 :- In the Partly Affirmative.

Issue No.3 :-
In the partly Affirmative.
Issue No.4 :- As per final order for the following.

:REASONS:
9. ISSUE No.1:

Before going to discuss Issue No.1 it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009)
13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others,
wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied".
Therefore it is crystal clear that the petitioners have to prove their case based on preponderance of probabilities.

10. According to the petitioners, on 13.04.2023 at about 9.45 a.m., Sandeep was proceeding by riding Honda Activa Bike bearing No. KA.11.EK.5856 on Halaguru-Channapattana road, near Naripura village, at that time the driver of the Ashoka Layland Goods Vehicle bearing No.
KA.42.A.9194 came from Halaguru side towards Channapattana at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the vehicle in which Sandeep was proceeding and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, Sandeep sustained grievous head injuries.

Immediately, injured was shifted to Halaguru Government Hospital, after first aid he was shifted to Chandramma Dayananda Sagar hospital, Harohalli and later he took treatment at Victoria hospital as an inpatient.
But inspite of treatment also injured succumbed to the accidental injuries on 14.04.2023.
To prove their contention, petitioners have lead oral and documentary evidence.
11. The 2nd petitioner, who is the brother of the deceased has examined himself as P.W.1 and filed affidavit by way of examination in chief and reiterated the averments made in the petition.
He also produced 17 documents, which were marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.17.

4 12.
In order to answer Issue No.1, it is appropriate to take Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11 for discussion.
Ex.P.1 is the true copy of FIR pertaining to Cr.No56/2023.

is the true copy of FSL report and Ex.P10 is the true copy of MLC register extract and Ex.P11 is the true copy of Charge Sheet.

13. According to respondents No.2, the alleged accident was occurred due to negligent riding of the rider of Motor Cycle in which the deceased was proceeding and also the deceased himself who was not wearing ISI mark headgear at the time of accident.
There was no negligence on the part of the driver of above said Ashok Leyland Goods Vehicle bearing No. KA.42.A.9194 for the cause accident.

In order to prove the same respondents have not lead any evidence.
14.
In order to prove the alleged negligence on the part of rider of motor cycle, respondent No.2 has cross-examined the P.W.1 in detail.
Nothing has been elicited from mouth of P.W.1 to establish that the accident was took place only on the negligence of rider of two wheeler in which the deceased was proceeding.
Hence, the respondent No.2 has failed to establish the negligence on the part of the deceased.

15. At this juncture it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2003 Karnataka page 493, between Mallamma Vs. Balaji and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held at para 12 as hereunder:
" Filing of the charge sheet against the driver is also a prima-facie case to hold that,
the driver of the said lorry was responsible for the accident and burden shifts on him to prove the same".
16.
In the instant case, the petitioners have produced police documents.
As per Ex.P.2, complaint was lodged before the Halaguru Police Station.
Thereafter, as per Ex.P.1, FIR was lodged against the driver of Ashok Leyland Goods Vehicle bearing No. KA.42.A.9194.
After through investigation, the investigating officer has filed charge sheet as per Ex.P11.

On careful perusal of Ex.P.1, Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.11, it appears to this Tribunal that, on the basis of complaint, the police have registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle and Investigating officer has submitted Charge sheet as per Ex.P.11 after completing investigation.
A careful perusal of Ex.P.8, it clearly goes to show that,
deceased
was died due to head injury in the RTA.

Further, on perusal of Ex.P.11 i.e., charge sheet, it reveals that, the driver of offending vehicle i.e., Ashok Leyland Goods Vehicle bearing No.
KA.42.A.9194 has been arrayed as an accused No.1.

The above referred decision is aptly applicable to the case on hand.
17.

Therefore, it is manifest that, the materials placed on record by the petitioners is sufficient to believe that, the accident took place due to rash or negligent driving of the driver of the Ashok Leyland Goods Vehicle bearing No. KA.42.A.9194.

At the cost of repetition, the contents of complaint and charge sheet clearly reveals that when the deceased was proceeding as a rider on the two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA.11.EK.5856, the driver of Ashok Leyland Goods Vehicle bearing No.

5 KA.42.A.9194 drove the said vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle in which the deceased was proceeding.

sentences.text: Due to which the deceased fell down from the motor cycle and sustained head injuries and other injuries and also succumbed to injuries while taking treatment.
The evidence placed on record clearly reveals that driver of Ashok Leyland Goods Vehicle bearing No. KA.42.A.9194 has caused the accident.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

18. ISSUE No.2:-
(a) Age:
According to the petitioners, the age of deceased was 34 years at the time of his death.
As per Ex.P-12- the Aadhaar Card of deceased and it reveals that, the date of birth of the deceased is 01.01.1989.
The accident was occurred on 13.04.2023.
Hence age of deceased is considered as 34 years at the time of his death.
(b) Income of the deceased:- Respondent Nos.2 has disputed the income of deceased.
P.W.1 has deposed that deceased was doing Agricultural work and also electrician work and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
However, to substantiate the exact income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents.

At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka decided in M.F.A. No.101144 of 2020 ( MV-I) on 05.07.2023, between Ananda Vs. Arun and Another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Para 9 (b) as hereunder:
"
In the absence of any cogent material on record, it is for the courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant".
In the instant case also, the petitioners have not produced the documents to establish the income of deceased.

As such in the absence of reliable document and supportive evidence, the notional income of the deceased is to be considered by relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka referred to above.
As per the notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident in the year 2022 is Rs.15,500/- per month.
It is pertinent to note that, the accident took place on 13.04.2023.
Hence, the notional income of the deceased is considered as Rs.16,000/- per month by adopting the method of KSLSA.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the partly Affirmative.
19. ISSUE No.3:-
This issue is with regard to entitlement of relief.
According to the petition averments, petitioner No.1 is the mother, petitioner No.2 is the brother and petitioner No.3 is the sister of deceased.
The 1st petitioner has lost her son and other petitioners have lost their loving brother.
Moreover, the bond between the parents and siblings is an eternal.

At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered in M.F.A.No.102868 of 2014 (M.V.D.), between Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Gangappa Saunshi and Others,
Thayamma vs Ameer Jan.S on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103404878/
6 wherein the Hon'ble High Court held that, "even if the dependency is relevant criteria to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency and the dependency includes gratuitous service dependency, physical dependency, emotional dependency and psychological dependency so on and so forth, which can never be equated in terms of the money.

entities.text:
Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Gangappa Saunshi and Others,
Thayamma vs Ameer Jan.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even married sons and daughters are entitled for compensation not only on conventional heads, but also on loss of dependency".
Hence, Petitioner Nos.1 to 3 are considered as dependents of deceased.
20. Already this Tribunal has observed that, as on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 43 years.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, held that "if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospects has to be taken into consideration while awarding compensation".

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is relevant to note that The Hon'ble Apex Court has provided the chart for the age of the deceased and percentage of future prospects as hereunder:
"If the deceased is self employed or fixed salary, his age below 40 years, future prospects is 40%".
"If the deceased between 40 to 50 years age, future prospects is 25%".
"If the deceased between 50 to 60 years age, future prospects is 10% and if the deceased more than 60 years, no addition as future prospects".
21. In this case the income of the deceased is considered as Rs.16,000/- per month.
The deceased was aged about 34 years and therefore, additional income is added to the income towards future prospects.
Hence, the future prospects of 40% is to be added to the income of deceased.
By applying the principles of above ruling, 40% of the income of Rs.16,000/- is Rs.6,400/-.

By adding the said amount with Rs.16,000/-, monthly income of deceased would be Rs.22,400/- (i.e., Rs.16,000 +
Rs.6,400/-).
In this case petitioner Nos.1 to 3 are considered as dependents of deceased.
Keeping in view of the deceased as a bachelor, 1/2 of the amount is to be deducted towards personal expenses of deceased.

After deducting 1/2 from Rs.22,400/- the actual monthly income would be Rs.11,200/-
(i.e, Rs.22,400 - Rs.11,200).

Then, total income of the deceased per annum would be Rs.1,34,400/-
(Rs.11,200/- x 12).
22.
The deceased was 34 years old at the time of death, the multiplier 16 is applied, which is appropriate to the age of deceased.

Then the loss of dependency is calculated as hereunder:
Rs.1,34,400/- X 16 = Rs.21,50,400/-.
Therefore, this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant compensation of Rs.21,50,400/- under the head of loss of dependency.

23. The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others has laid down the guidelines with regard to awarding compensation towards loss of estate, funeral expenses and consortium.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners have contended that, they have spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies expenses.

In order to substantiate the same, they Thayamma vs Ameer Jan.S on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103404878/
7 have not produced any documents.

sentences.text: Now the question before this Tribunal is whether petitioner Nos.1 to 3 are also entitled for consortium or not?
Admittedly, the 1 st petitioner is the mother and she is entitled for filial consortium.
Admittedly the petitioner Nos.2 & 3 are the brother and sister of deceased.
At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2018 (1) SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nanuram @ Churu Ram and Others.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nanuram @ Churu Ram and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court held that, the parents and children are having right to get the compensation under filial consortium.
Therefore, the petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for Rs.48,000/- each under the head of consortium.
Further, Rs.18,000/- is awarded for funeral expenses and also Rs.18,000/- is awarded towards loss of estate.

24. The details of compensation amount is as under:

 1. Towards loss of Rs. 21,50,400/-
 Dependency.
 2. Towards consortium Rs. 1,44,000/-
 48,000 X 3  3. Loss of Estate Rs. 18,000/-
 4. Funeral expense Rs. 18,000/-
Total Rs

Hence, petitioners are entitled for just and reasonable amount of Rs.23,30,400/-.
25.
Regarding liability:
Driving License:-
According to respondent No.2, the driver of Ashok Leyland Goods Vehicle bearing No. KA.42.A.9194 was not holding valid driving licence to drive the same at the time of accident.
However Charge sheet submitted by IO does not reveals that driver of offending vehicle was driving the vehicle without valid and effective DL.
Hence, it appears to this tribunal that, the driver of offending vehicle was holding valid and effective D.L. as on the date of alleged accident.
Insurance Policy:-

In the instant case, respondent No.2 has admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to Ashok Leyland Goods Vehicle bearing No.
KA.42.A.9194.
Hence, the respondent No.2 shall pay compensation amount to the petitioner.
Interest:

In view of the decision reported in MFA NO: 30131-2019 dtd, 12.5.2020 and M.F.A.No.100090/2014 C/w M.F.A.No.25107/2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and Others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and Another, rate of interest on the compensation amount is awarded at 6% p.a. from the date of petition.

Accordingly,
Issue No.2 is answered in the Partly Affirmative.

Issue No.5:-.
In view of discussion made above, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following.

:ORDER:
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the Petition.
Petitioners are awarded just and reasonable compensation of Rs. 23,30,400/-
(Rupees Twenty three lakhs thirty thousand and four hundred Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the court.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and directed to deposit the compensation amount awarded to the petitioners in the Tribunal within 2 months from the date of this judgment.
Draw award accordingly.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
: APPORTIONMENT OF COMPENSATION :
On deposit of compensation amount, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for 80% and petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are entitled for 10% each with interest.

50% of share of petitioner No.1 with interest is to be paid to her through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification as per rules and after verifying the stay order from the Hon'ble Appellate Court and remaining 50% of her share with interest shall be invested in F.D. in her name in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank of her choice for a period of 3 years.
It is clarified that, the 1 st petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.
Entire share of petitioner Nos.2 and 3 with interest is to be paid to them through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification as per rules.

1.
Whether petitioners proves that Sandeep L S was died on 14.04.2023 in the accident occurred on 13.04.2023 at 9.45 a.m. near Nareepura village, on Halaguru - Channapatna road, due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Ashok Layland Lorry bearing No. KA.42.A.9194 as stated in the petition?
Thayamma vs Ameer Jan.S on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103404878/
3
2. Whether the petitioners prove the age and income of the deceased?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation? If so, how much and from whom ?
4. What order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In the instant case, the petitioners have produced police documents.
As per Ex.P.2, complaint was lodged before the Halaguru Police Station.
Thereafter, as per Ex.P.1, FIR was lodged against the driver of Ashok Leyland Goods Vehicle bearing No. KA.42.A.9194.
After through investigation, the investigating officer has filed charge sheet as per Ex.P11.
On careful perusal of Ex.P.1, Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.11, it appears to this Tribunal that, on the basis of complaint, the police have registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle and Investigating officer has submitted Charge sheet as per Ex.P.11 after completing investigation.
A careful perusal of Ex.P.8, it clearly goes to show that,
was died due to head injury in the RTA.
Further, on perusal of Ex.P.11 i.e., charge sheet, it reveals that, the driver of offending vehicle i.e., Ashok Leyland Goods Vehicle bearing No.
KA.42.A.9194 has been arrayed as an accused No.1.
Therefore, it is manifest that, the materials placed on record by the petitioners is sufficient to believe that, the accident took place due to rash or negligent driving of the driver of the Ashok Leyland Goods Vehicle bearing No. KA.42.A.9194.
Due to which the deceased fell down from the motor cycle and sustained head injuries and other injuries and also succumbed to injuries while taking treatment.
In the instant case also, the petitioners have not produced the documents to establish the income of deceased.
As such in the absence of reliable document and supportive evidence, the notional income of the deceased is to be considered by relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka referred to above.
The 1st petitioner has lost her son and other petitioners have lost their loving brother.
Moreover, the bond between the parents and siblings is an eternal.
21. In this case the income of the deceased is considered as Rs.16,000/- per month.
The deceased was aged about 34 years and therefore, additional income is added to the income towards future prospects.
Hence, the future prospects of 40% is to be added to the income of deceased.
In this case petitioner Nos.1 to 3 are considered as dependents of deceased.
23. The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others has laid down the guidelines with regard to awarding compensation towards loss of estate, funeral expenses and consortium.
The Hon'ble Apex Court held that, the parents and children are having right to get the compensation under filial consortium.

Therefore, the petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for Rs.48,000/- each under the head of consortium.
Further, Rs.18,000/- is awarded for funeral expenses and also Rs.18,000/- is awarded towards loss of estate.
